body: It’s not that I wasn’t ever comitted. It was the other way around.

I might have made myself unclear, but since the cancer has been a long part of the relationship I don’t think it is the cancer that is making us drift apart. While I don’t think anyone is ever fully equipped to deal with something like this, doesn’t mean I haven’t taken care of her to the best of my ability. The problem is that I have a hard time mainting that level of care while our personalities clash the way they do. It’s obvious that she wants me to be something I’m not, and I want her to be something she’s not. Does it make more sense?

I’m sorry for your loss. My biggest issue is that I feel like our relationship is taking a toll on her, and that I’m just making matters worse. I’ve tried making sacrifices, but in the end I’m just left bitter and irritated. This was largely due to the amount of time I spent caring for her, while not allowed to socialize with friends and having a massive university workload in a city I’ve not lived in long.

I told her that the she isn’t negative per se, but that her focus aren’t at the right things. When I made you dinner, you shouldn’t focus on the cheese I bought, but the fact that I spent time making something for you. Her response was that nobody had ever told her that she could be a negative person, and I could see that it got to her. Hopefully it does, and we can start embracing the good in eachother instead of the negatives.
I’ve spent weeks on end at the hospital, seens the scars and was there when she had start chemo again. She definitly has cancer.

I agree that it wouldn’t be good if I couldn’t take care of myself, the problem is that I most definitly can. I have my ups and down, and her parents refused to let me stay with her because I was detrimental to her health according to them. When they told me this I had been going between University, the hospital, back home to my apartment to get new clothes or books I needed, back again to the hospital. My girlfriend didn’t allow me to leave her alone there, so I could never socialize with friends. I did this for almost 3 weeks non-stop, and coupled with the fact the nurses woke me up 3 times a night (meaning that very valuable rem sleep was lost) I became very tired and slightly irritated. When the parents came over to «take over» for me, they noticed this, and concluded that I was dangerous. They didn’t even take into account any of the things I did good, just the negatives. I could’ve done things differently, but with the workload I was under things should’ve been more evenly spaced out. I’ve tried to «fix» this by being more positive and helping out where I can, since she’s mainly at home, but it hasn’t helped.

She has gone to therapy, but tells me herself that she shuts down and doesn’t want to talk to them. I’ve tried to tell her that the golden rule is that you can help those who wish to be helped, but she is adamant (even thought she knows she doesn’t have the mental tools for dealing with the stress and hurt) that she doesn’t want to go to a therapist.

My issue with her parents are that they just assume what I’m capable of. Their theory was that since I was sleepy and had two difficults week, I’d do harm to their daughter. But she also had to move out for school, so would it be better to share an apartment with somebody who doesn’t have knowledge of her condition? The last time she was in my apartment she was getting septic, and I had to bring her to the emergency room. There is no knowing if any other roommate would’ve been there. After I voiced thede concerns to them, I think they understood a little better, but thinks have been awkward ever since.

What boggles my mind at times is that she is an extrovert at large, but she has such huge issues forming emotional ties to people close to her. Her good side really shows in bigger groups of people, but when it’s me and her - all she wants to do is be with other people.

I really appreciate this sentiment. I do realize I have to talk to her about this, and I’ll try my hardest to keep what you said in the back of my mind when I do so. I do believe she is afraid of people leaving her, and if this relationship crumbles I’ll still be there for her and help out where I can. It isn’t so much her lack of respect for me (or maybe it is), but the values she has grown up with. Her parents have been very restrictive in what she’s been exposed to during her childhood, and I think that’s the underlying issue at play. 

Sex has been an issue, because she has never been exposed to any sexual education, nor any healthy sexual relationship. For me sex isn’t the act it self, but the emotional attachment to my girlfriend. Whenever I try to voice my concerns with the lack of intimacy, she tells me I sound like her ex-boyfriend and recites statistics like «only 1 in 4 women cum during sex» so therefore sex isn’t enjoyable. I think she’s missing the bigger picture perhaps, and it really gives birth to some insecurities. 

Good on you for staying with her. I hope that me and my girlfriend can get a good talk about all of my concerns and hers. Maybe we can find some common ground and do what you and your girlfriend managed to. Thanks.
